senses.gloss: (b. h.) to cover.—Part. pass. כָּסוּי, f. כְּסוּיָה; pl. כְּסוּיִים, כְּסוּיִין; כְּסוּיוֹת.
units: <cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 52">Gen. R. s. 52</cite> <he>אתם כִּסִּיתֶם … כְּסוּי עינים</he> you have concealed from me the sight (of truth), therefore the son that you will raise will be of covered eyes (blind); <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 91:3">Yalk. Gen. 91</cite> <cite ref="K00911"><he>כסות</he></cite> (corr. acc.); <cite ref="Bava Kamma 93a:5">B. Kam. 93ᵃ</cite> <he>הואיל וכִיסִּית … בנים כְּסוּיֵי עיניים</he> (v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note).
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Terumot 8:3:21">Y. Ter. VIII, 45ᵈ</cite> <he>הכְּסוּיִין</he> (not <he>הכיסוין</he>) the covered liquids.
<cite ref="Mishnah Chullin 6:4">Ḥull. VI, 4</cite> … <he>שחט ולא כ׳ לכַסּוֹת</he> if one slaughters and fails to cover the blood, and another person sees it, he is bound to cover it.

<cite ref="Pesachim 119a:2">Pes. 119ᵃ</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Isaiah 23:18">Is. XXIII, 18</cite>) <he>זהו המְכַסֶּה דברים וכ׳</he> he who keeps secret the things which the Old of Days has covered (mysteries). B. Kam. l. c.; Gen. R. l. c., v. supra.
<cite ref="Pesikta Rabbati 26:1">Pesik. R. s. 26</cite> <he>מְכַסָּה אני ממך</he> shall I conceal it from thee?—
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 87:5">Gen. R. s. 87</cite> <he>כִּסְּתָה פניה</he> she covered her (the idol’s) face.

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 87:5">Ib.</cite> <he>לא כ׳ עליהם הכתוב</he> the Bible did not cover their guilt (v. <cite ref="H01423"><he>חָפָה</he></cite>); a. fr.—Part. pass. <he>מְכוּסֶּה</he>, f. <he>מְכוּסָּה</he>; pl. <he>מְכוּסִּים</he>, <he>מְכוּסִּין</he>; <he>מְכוּסּוֹת</he>.

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 87:5">Ib.</cite> s. 52 (ref. to <cite ref="Genesis 20:16">Gen. XX, 16</cite> [read:] <he>עשאה מטרונה כסות עינים שהיא מכ׳ מן העין</he> he (Abimelech) made a matron of her (Sarah) (giving her) ‘a cover of the eyes’, by which she was protected from the gaze (of men).

<cite ref="Pesachim 54b:2">Pes. 54ᵇ</cite> <he>שבעה … מכ׳ וכ׳</he> seven things are hidden from man; a. fr.—[<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 79">Gen. R. s. 79</cite>, end <he>מה את מכסה בי</he>, read: <he>מב׳</he>, v. <cite ref="B00971"><he>בְּסָא</he></cite>.—Sifra B’ḥuck., Par. 2, ch. V <cite ref="K00917"><he>כיסה</he></cite>, v. <cite ref="K00913"><he>כָּסַח</he></cite>.]

<cite ref="Mishnah Sanhedrin 2:1">Snh. II, 1</cite> (<cite ref="Sanhedrin 18a">18ᵃ</cite>; <cite ref="Sanhedrin 19a:4">19ᵃ</cite>) <he>הן נִכְסִין … והוא נ׳</he> when they (who form the funeral cortege) are hidden from his view (when entering an alley), he (the high priest) appears; when they emerge, he disappears (in the alley).
<cite ref="Shir HaShirim Rabbah 2:9">Cant. R. to II, 9</cite> <he>נראה וחוזר ונ׳</he> is visible and disappears again; Ruth. R. to II, 14; Pesik. Haḥod., p. 49ᵇ.
<cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 22">Num. R. s. 22</cite> (play on <cite ref="N00841"><he>נְכָסִים</he></cite>) <he>נ׳ מזה וכ׳</he> they disappear from one and appear to the other; a. fr.

<cite ref="Beitzah 16a:2">Bets. 16ᵃ</cite> (ref. to <he>בַּכֶּסֶה</he>, <cite ref="Psalms 81:4">Ps. LXXXI, 4</cite>) <he>איזהו חג שהחדש מִתְכַּסֶּה בו</he> what festival is that on which the new moon is hidden (seen only by a few)?; <cite ref="Pirkei DeRabbi Eliezer 7">Pirké d’R. El. ch. VII</cite>, end <he>ביום שמ׳ כולו</he> on the day when the moon is entirely covered.
<cite ref="Devarim Rabbah 3">Deut. R. s. 3</cite> <he>מתכ׳ משלו</he> clothed himself at his (the fosterfather’s) expense.
<cite ref="Devarim Rabbah 3">Ib.</cite> <he>כל … אוכל ומתכ׳ וכ׳</he> all that is spent on you for eating and clothing &c.
<cite ref="Mishnah Tamid 1:1">Tam. I, 1</cite> <he>מִתְכַּסִּין</he>, v. <cite ref="K00911"><he>כְּסוּת</he></cite>; a. fr.
